A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EventWeave. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support comparison, including matching relocated material. No essential reading gaps remain.

before.justification: v1 reports original response-generation, event-retrieval, deletion-robustness, ablation, and human-evaluation results on CC and MSC in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original results on CC, MSC, and LoCoMo, including additional memory comparisons, retrieval and relationship ablations, scalability measurements, and human evaluation.

M1.justification: v2 adds learned node-retention decisions using an LSTM future-reference predictor and policy-gradient weights, and modifies connectivity preservation with a learned compatibility cost (Section 3.3). Section 4 also specifies recency/relevance/PageRank retrieval with dynamic mixing and decoder conditioning, beyond v1's general event-node retrieval description.

E1.justification: v2 retains CC and MSC and adds evaluated LoCoMo dialogues, extending coverage to substantially longer conversations with distant references and interleaved topics (Table 1). The newly named encoder-training datasets are treated as implementation disclosure, since v1 left its dialogue-training data unspecified.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated MemWalker, LongMem, and LifeLongMem comparisons and removes LongCoT from the reported comparison suite. Backtracking and human comparisons shift from multiple backbone models to GPT-4o memory variants. The additional LoCoMo comparator's identity is unclear: Table 1 calls it DialogLM, while Section 5.1 and Figure 3 use LD-Agent.

E3.justification: The reported response metric changes from BLEU-3 to BLEU-4, and main event scores change from CC-centered reporting to three-dataset averages. v2 replaces much of the backbone/model-size evaluation with Qwen3-14B, GPT-o1, and DeepSeek variants, and adds few-shot response-generation, dialogue-length stratification, and resource-measurement protocols. These reported changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 expands component ablations and adds retrieval-perspective isolation, relationship-type removal/addition, dialogue-length, and pruning/resource analyses (Tables 2, 4, 10–13). It adds the missing-cat case study. The original threshold analysis, ICL retrieval curves, and full boat-building case are retained in the appendices rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix D newly reports three raters per example and inter-annotator agreement using Fleiss' kappa, 0.72. v1 supplies neither detail. The existing ICL mean/min–max bands remain; neither version reports experimental seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive LoCoMo, memory-baseline, few-shot, ablation, efficiency, and human-evaluation results, while removing v1's standalone retrieval comparison table and much of its model-size sweep. Retained configurations also have revised values: Qwen2.5-14B with EventWeave has CC ROUGE-L 46.0 in v1 Table 11 versus 44.2 in v2 Table 8. Revised methods and settings prevent treating these differences as controlled performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: v2 substantially extends the mathematical specification with a node-utility definition, a revised connectivity-path objective, and formal retrieval scoring and decoder conditioning (Equations 10–17). These go beyond equivalent notation or explanation of v1's mathematics. The event-metric formulas in Appendix A.3 remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction shift the contribution emphasis from identifying supporting events and maintaining context to selective relationship modeling, concise natural responses, and demonstrated efficiency and scalability. v2 additionally claims that ablations establish benefits from event relationships rather than increased information density. These extend the scientific claims beyond the largely retained conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations assigning complementary roles to semantic relevance, recency, and graph structure; argues that three relationship types usually suffice; and identifies highly rhetorical discourse as a possible exception. Appendix B.4 develops a pruning/resource/quality tradeoff where v1 primarily offered a general graph-growth warning. The main limitations paragraph also softens that warning.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies the BERT encoder, DailyDialog/OpenDialKG training data, classifier and segmentation details, and attention-weight computation. Appendix A.4 discloses a 4k-token context, 30-node limit, final-session testing, and at most five previous sessions. Appendix D adds annotator and sample counts and blinding details. These materially expand documentation without establishing changes to previously unspecified settings.

R1.justification: Section 2 is substantially repositioned around dialogue-context management and inference through structured prompts. v2 adds discussion of Graph of Thoughts, GraphText, and Ctrl-Struct, alongside new memory-method and LoCoMo citations. This changes the relationship to prior research beyond bibliographic updates; updated or duplicated Li and Ong entries are not counted as distinct new works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and substantial method and experimental prose are rewritten. Graph construction and hierarchical maintenance are consolidated into Section 3, response generation receives Section 4, and analyses are reorganized into expanded appendices. These are extensive narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: v2 combines response and event results into wider multi-dataset tables, adds efficiency, dialogue-length, retrieval, and relationship displays, and replaces the main human-evaluation plot with an appendix table. The ICL and threshold plots move to the appendices. Figures 1–2 retain their artwork, although Figure 2's caption changes substantially.

improvement.justification: Broader memory comparisons, diagnostic analyses, and implementation and human-study disclosures address important omissions in v1. However, v1's GPT-4o ProactiveCoT result tuple appears under vanilla in v2 Table 1 despite the BLEU change, and the LoCoMo comparator is inconsistently named. Appendix B.4.3 also claims a 3% pruning memory reduction where Table 11's 63-to-54 KB implies 14.3%. These unresolved reporting problems affect important new evidence, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
